req.title: Create new post
req.statement: The system shall insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user when POST /create receives a title and body, then redirect to /.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /create must insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user and redirect to /. I design: (1) a positive EP test confirming 302 redirect and DB row insertion with correct author_id; (2) a negative NEG test confirming unauthenticated access redirects to login (not /create); (3) a boundary BVA test with minimum-length title ('A') and body ('A') confirming acceptance; (4) a negative DT test confirming empty title is rejected and no row inserted; (5) a STC test confirming the full state transition: unauthenticated -> login -> authenticated -> create -> redirect to index. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill operator-flip and constant-bump mutations.

tests.name: test_create_post_authenticated_inserts_row_and_redirects
preconditions: App initialized with test database containing pre-loaded users
User Rahul (id=1, password='stone') exists in DB
User is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /create with title='Test Post Title' and body='Test post body content'
expected: Exactly one new post row exists in DB with title='Test Post Title' and author_id=1
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_create_post_authenticated_inserts_row_and_redirects():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Test Post Title', 'body': 'Test post body content'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        db = get_db()
        row = db.execute("SELECT * FROM post WHERE title = 'Test Post Title'").fetchone()
        assert row is not None
        assert row['title'] == 'Test Post Title'
        assert row['body'] == 'Test post body content'
        assert row['author_id'] == 1

actions: POST /create with title='Some Title' and body='Some body' without logging in
expected: No new post row inserted in DB

def test_create_post_unauthenticated_redirects_to_login():

tests.name: test_create_post_state_transition_unauth_to_auth_to_created
preconditions: User Ishaan (id=3, password='stone') exists in DB
actions: POST /create with valid title and body (state: post created)
GET / to verify post appears in index
expected: New post with author_id=3 exists in DB
GET / returns 200 and contains the new post title
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_create_post_state_transition_unauth_to_auth_to_created():
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Ishaan Unique Post', 'body': 'Ishaan body text'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        row = get_db().execute("SELECT * FROM post WHERE title = 'Ishaan Unique Post'").fetchone()
        assert row is not None
        assert row['author_id'] == 3
        assert row['body'] == 'Ishaan body text'
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Ishaan Unique Post' in r.data
